title: What does it mean to "understand math"?

cues.en: Everyone.
cues.zh: 大家好。

cues.en: This is the first tangent video.
cues.zh: 這是第一支岔題影片。

cues.en: And so I'm going to start this video by saying a few quick words about these tangent sections.
cues.zh: 所以影片一開始，我先簡單說明一下這些岔題單元。

cues.en: I like to have these occasional brief discussions that are not exactly in the topic of the course, but are more general to try to answer the question of why you are here.
cues.zh: 我喜歡偶爾安排簡短討論，內容不完全屬於課程主題，而是從更廣的角度，試著回答你為什麼來到這裡。

cues.en: Well, okay, that's a big question.
cues.zh: 好吧，這是個大哉問。

cues.en: I don't mean why do you exist and what is the purpose of life?
cues.zh: 我不是在問你為什麼存在，以及人生的意義是什麼。

cues.en: I mean, why are you here watching this course?
cues.zh: 我是說，你為什麼來看這門課？

cues.en: So these little tangent sections are my opportunity to say a few things that I hope you will find interesting and thought provoking.
cues.zh: 所以這些小小的岔題單元，讓我有機會談一些希望你會覺得有趣、值得思考的事情。

cues.en: These are like meta discussions about the course and more generally about mathematics and online education.
cues.zh: 有點像是針對課程本身，以及更廣泛的數學和線上教育所做的討論。

cues.en: I hope you enjoy these tangent videos, but just to be clear, they're absolutely not critical to the
cues.zh: 希望你喜歡這些岔題影片，但先說清楚，它們並不是

cues.en: course material, so you can safely skip these tangent videos if you really just want to focus exclusively on the math and the coding material.
cues.zh: 課程教材的必要部分。所以如果你只想專注在數學和程式內容，可以放心跳過這些影片。

cues.en: But I will try to keep these videos short and interesting.
cues.zh: 不過我會盡量讓影片簡短又有趣。

cues.en: So I do hope that you stay for them.
cues.zh: 所以還是希望你留下來看看。

cues.en: Now you don't need to reply or really do anything, but if you have some thoughts or reactions or feelings
cues.zh: 你不需要回覆或做任何事，但如果有想法、反應或感受，

cues.en: that you would like to share with your fellow learners in this course or with me, then feel free to post your thoughts to the Q&A for this video.
cues.zh: 想和這門課的其他學員或我分享，歡迎把想法貼到這支影片的問答區。

cues.en: And so with this as a general introduction to this type of video, let me begin this lecture.
cues.zh: 以上是這類影片的一般介紹，現在就開始這堂課。

cues.en: The purpose of this video is to discuss the different ways that you can understand mathematics and to
cues.zh: 這支影片要討論的是理解數學的不同方式，並且

cues.en: encourage you to try to think about which level of understanding math is right for you based on your goals and your time constraints and your intentions.
cues.zh: 鼓勵你根據自己的目標、時間限制與意圖，思考哪一種理解數學的層次適合你。

cues.en: So the question at hand is what does it actually mean to understand math?
cues.zh: 所以眼前的問題是：理解數學，究竟是什麼意思？

cues.en: Here.
cues.zh: 這裡，

cues.en: I have a list of different ways of understanding math.
cues.zh: 我列出了幾種理解數學的方式。

cues.en: Now, these are not the same, and they're also not mutually exclusive, of course.
cues.zh: 當然，這些方式並不相同，也不是互斥的。

cues.en: But, you know, you can have, for example, a good conceptual grasp of how different functions behave
cues.zh: 例如，你可能很能從概念上掌握不同函數的行為，

cues.en: without being able to derive them from elementary proofs and first principles.
cues.zh: 卻不會從基本證明與第一原理推導它們。

cues.en: And one example is a Gaussian, the so called bell curve function.
cues.zh: 高斯函數，也就是所謂的鐘形曲線，就是一個例子。

cues.en: I'm sure you're familiar with it, even if you're not familiar with the formula, it looks something like this.
cues.zh: 我相信你認得它，即使不熟悉公式。它看起來大概像這樣。

cues.en: It starts off close to zero.
cues.zh: 一開始接近零，

cues.en: It goes up and then it goes back down.
cues.zh: 往上升，然後再降下來。

cues.en: Now you can understand the behavior, the characteristics of this function, and maybe you can if you
cues.zh: 你可以理解這個函數的行為與特性，而且如果你

cues.en: study statistics, you will understand the importance of this function in probability theory, even though you might not be able to derive the function from first principles.
cues.zh: 學過統計，也會明白它在機率論中的重要性，即使你未必能從第一原理推導出這個函數。

cues.en: And that's totally fine.
cues.zh: 這完全沒有問題。

cues.en: You do not need to be able to derive this function from scratch in order to use it.
cues.zh: 並不是要能從頭推導這個函數，才能使用它。

cues.en: So you can have intuition for how functions behave, why they are important for applications in statistics or financial modeling or sound engineering or deep learning.
cues.zh: 所以你可以對函數的行為建立直覺，理解它們為什麼對統計、金融建模、音訊工程或深度學習的應用很重要。

cues.en: And you know, there's also historical and philosophical contexts in which mathematicians worked and
cues.zh: 此外，數學家是在特定的歷史與哲學脈絡中工作，

cues.en: developed these ideas, and you can learn all about that if you find it interesting.
cues.zh: 發展出這些想法的。如果有興趣，也可以深入了解。

cues.en: Again, you can know a lot about the history of math without being able to visualize equations and hence sketch equations.
cues.zh: 同樣地，你可能很了解數學史，卻不會把方程式視覺化、畫出圖形。

cues.en: Here, let me give you an example to make this a little more concrete.
cues.zh: 我舉個例子，讓這件事更具體。

cues.en: So there's three things on this slide.
cues.zh: 這張投影片上有三種東西。

cues.en: There's code, there's actually MATLAB code.
cues.zh: 有程式碼，實際上是 MATLAB 程式碼。

cues.en: It's not Python code.
cues.zh: 不是 Python 程式碼。

cues.en: This is MATLAB code, but doesn't matter.
cues.zh: 這是 MATLAB，不過沒關係。

cues.en: There's code, there's English text and there's some math equations.
cues.zh: 有程式碼、有英文文字，也有數學方程式。

cues.en: Now, all three of these things are different representations of exactly the same underlying phenomenon.
cues.zh: 這三者其實都在用不同方式，表達完全相同的底層現象。

cues.en: It's the same underlying process, and we can understand it with code, we can understand it with written language and we can understand it with math functions.
cues.zh: 它們描述的是同一個過程；可以用程式碼理解、用文字理解，也可以用數學函數理解。

cues.en: Now, none of these is intrinsically better or worse.
cues.zh: 這幾種方式，本質上都沒有比較好或比較差。

cues.en: They are simply different levels of understanding that are more or less useful for different applications or for different individuals with different backgrounds and different goals.
cues.zh: 它們只是不同層次的理解，對不同應用，或不同背景、目標的人，各有不同的用處。

cues.en: And that's really the point that I want to make here.
cues.zh: 這就是我真正想強調的。

cues.en: You know, if your goal is to get a PhD in abstract math, then yeah, you'd better learn how to construct proofs.
cues.zh: 如果你的目標是取得抽象數學博士學位，對，你最好學會怎麼建構證明。

cues.en: But if your goal is to become a data scientist working to improve self-driving cars, then do you really need to understand the abstractions of number theory?
cues.zh: 但如果你的目標是成為資料科學家，改善自駕車，你真的需要理解數論的抽象概念嗎？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不需要。

cues.en: You just need to have the right intuition for why gradient descent works, for example.
cues.zh: 例如，你只需要對梯度下降為什麼有效，建立正確的直覺。

cues.en: So this is an important issue because math is such a huge area of human knowledge and there are so many ways to learn math and to understand math.
cues.zh: 這是個重要的問題，因為數學是人類知識中極為廣大的領域，而且學習、理解數學的方式很多。

cues.en: So you should really take some time to figure out your own goals, why you want to understand math and what level is appropriate for you.
cues.zh: 所以你真的應該花點時間，釐清自己的目標、為什麼想理解數學，以及哪種層次適合你。

cues.en: And from there you can try to find the right courses or books that are suitable for your interests and your goals and your time constraints.
cues.zh: 再從這裡出發，尋找符合自己興趣、目標與時間限制的課程或書籍。

cues.en: Of course, I certainly hope that you find my courses useful, but I also know that my courses are not right for everyone.
cues.zh: 當然，我很希望你覺得我的課有幫助，但我也知道，我的課不可能適合每個人。

cues.en: Now you need to be realistic and and you should accept the reality that your goals and your targeted
cues.zh: 現在，你必須務實，也要接受：你的目標，以及希望達到的

cues.en: levels of understanding math might need to be updated periodically.
cues.zh: 數學理解層次，可能需要定期調整。

cues.en: For example, at the beginning of the course, it's easy to say that you're going to dedicate 30 hours
cues.zh: 例如，課程剛開始時，很容易說自己每週要花 30 小時，

cues.en: a week to studying math in a lot of depth, But well, when it comes down to it, 30 hours a week is
cues.zh: 深入學習數學。但實際上，每週 30 小時

cues.en: a lot, especially if you're also studying or working and doing a lot of different things in your life.
cues.zh: 真的很多，尤其是你還在讀書或工作，生活中也有很多其他事情時。

cues.en: And another thing I want to mention here is that it's important to compare yourself to the right people.
cues.zh: 我還想提到，和正確的對象比較很重要。

cues.en: Now, the advice that people always give is you should never compare yourself to others.
cues.zh: 大家常給的建議是，永遠不要拿自己和別人比較。

cues.en: But come on, let's be honest.
cues.zh: 但拜託，我們坦白一點。

cues.en: We're always comparing ourselves to other people.
cues.zh: 我們總是會把自己和別人比較。

cues.en: I'm not saying that's the healthiest way to be, but, you know, that's just the reality of how it is.
cues.zh: 我不是說這是最健康的做法，但現實就是這樣。

cues.en: So given this, just make sure that you are comparing yourself against the right group.
cues.zh: 既然如此，就要確保你拿來比較的群體是合適的。

cues.en: Don't be frustrated that you're not as math savvy as some math professor at Harvard.
cues.zh: 不要因為自己不像哈佛的數學教授那麼精通數學，就感到挫折。

cues.en: Actually, the best person to compare yourself to is you, your former, you you in the past.
cues.zh: 其實最好的比較對象是你自己，是以前的你、過去的你。

cues.en: So the question that you should be asking yourself is, do you understand calculus better today than you did six months ago?
cues.zh: 所以你應該問自己：今天的你，是否比六個月前更理解微積分？

cues.en: And finally, the last thing I want to mention is always remember that learning math and coding in particular together is pretty challenging.
cues.zh: 最後，我想說的是，請永遠記住，學習數學，尤其是同時學習數學與程式，確實很有挑戰性。

cues.en: It's hard, really.
cues.zh: 真的很難。

cues.en: These are not easy topics to learn.
cues.zh: 這些都不是容易學的主題。

cues.en: It's going to be difficult and it's going to be challenging at times.
cues.zh: 這個過程有時會很困難、很有挑戰性。

cues.en: And you just need to embrace and enjoy those challenges.
cues.zh: 你要做的，就是接受並享受這些挑戰。

cues.en: And in fact, I have an entire tangent video that's really just about this statement here.
cues.zh: 事實上，我有一整支岔題影片，就是在談這裡的這句話。

cues.en: That video is going to be later in the course.
cues.zh: 那支影片會在課程後面出現。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So that's it for this video.
cues.zh: 這支影片就到這裡。

cues.en: I hope I have inspired you to think about how you want to understand and apply math.
cues.zh: 希望我讓你開始思考，自己想如何理解與應用數學。

cues.en: If you have any reactions or thoughts that you'd like to share, feel free to post to the Q&A.
cues.zh: 如果你有想分享的感想或想法，歡迎貼到問答區。

cues.en: Otherwise, I will see you in the next section.
cues.zh: 不然，我們就在下一節見。
